about: Hand labels for the stratified sample emitted by semantic_coverage_probe.py. Labels were assigned by reading each clause against the retrieved ask's interpretation and its source quote. Codes: M = the register ask captures this clause's intent (a reader would accept it as the same ask); W = topically adjacent or partially overlapping, but a different or narrower intent; N = not captured. The scorer recomputes every published figure from this file, so no number in the docs is hand-carried.
labeller: agent (jcode), single labeller, no second rater
confidence_in_labels: high for N in the low band (transcription noise, unrelated ask); moderate for W (partial-overlap boundary is a judgement call and the M/W split is the main source of uncertainty in precision)

notes: The low band is uniformly transcription noise or social chatter with an unrelated retrieved ask, so the negative side of the detector is clean.
The high band is where the honest problem is: 8 of 30 top-ranked pairs are adjacent-but-different intents. A cosine threshold alone therefore cannot certify that a clause is captured.
Labels are one labeller's. A second rater has not been run, so the M/W boundary carries unmeasured disagreement.
